correctness.rationale: Assume a=gq,c=gr with gcd(q,r)=1 and q>1. Choose m divisible by ord_a(b), n_m=(b^m-1)/a, giving S_b(a n_m)=m(b-1). Let ell=ord_q(b), B=b^ell, write r=hq+s (1<=s<q), and A=s(B-1)/q integer in [1,B-2]. For m=K ell, X_K=s(b^m-1)/q has K equal base-B digits A; hence S_b(X_K)=K S_b(A)<=m(b-1)-K. Subtraction of fixed h borrows through at most bounded low blocks since A>0, and the high h*b^m block stays disjoint, so S_b(c n_m)<=m(b-1)-K+O(1), contradiction as K grows. Interchange a,c to prove equality. For prime p strip valuation powers which append zero digits, giving iff p-free cores equal. Repeated block identity checked on exact bounded instances, but proof is symbolic.
residual_risks: Proven for coprime multipliers in any integer base; fully arbitrary multipliers classified only for prime base.
